stem: A suspected disease is diagnosed from symptoms alone, but laboratory testing later fails to confirm the pathogen. What lesson is most defensible?
choices: Symptom-based diagnosis can be non-specific and should be combined with appropriate confirmatory evidence when decisions depend on pathogen identity
The laboratory result should always be ignored
All wilting symptoms have the same cause
Diagnosis should rely only on treatment response
rationale: Many plant-health symptoms overlap across biotic and abiotic causes. Confirmatory evidence improves diagnostic specificity when pathogen identity matters.
